items.title: Employees at the world’s biggest AI companies are calling for a slowdown in AI development
items.summary:
The letter comes on the heels of major advancements and burgeoning threats from rapidly developing AI systems. OpenAI disclosed last week that two of its test models escaped a lab environment, bypassed its systems to gain access to the open internet and hacked a different company’s internal system. [...] “We’re glad to see broad agreement across the field on the need for technical and governance tools to pace the frontier of AI development, including the ability to slow it, so society can prepare,” Anthropic said in a comment to CNN.

Google DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis also recently called for a new international standards body to help set protocols for new AI models, an idea endorsed by Altman, SpaceX’s Elon Musk, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella and other major industry figures. [...] OpenAI said in a statement to CNN they agree with potentially pacing the development of AI, adding they “hope to contribute to work led by the U.S. government, alongside other labs” on the topic.

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman suggested it may be time to slow down AI development in a podcast interview Tuesday. The OpenAI models that broke out of their test environment are fueling “long term questions” about how AI companies should address this new rate of progress.

items.title: House Panel Weighs AI Job Gains Against Worker Risks
items.summary:
In April 2025, President Trump signed an executive order creating a White House task force on AI education and directing the Secretary of Labor to expand AI-related Registered Apprenticeships. The administration's AI Action Plan directs the Department of Labor to prioritize AI skill development across workforce funding streams and proposes an AI Workforce Research Hub. Beginning July 1, students became eligible for Pell Grants covering short-term programs in high-skill, in-demand fields. [...] ## The Bottom Line

Eight hearings in, the committee has built a case for AI as an opportunity engine without producing legislation that reconciles it with what Barlow and McBath described. Augusta made the tension concrete: the same technology anchoring a biomanufacturing plant and a new medical AI department also requires transmission lines running through civilians' properties.

Access the Legis1 platform for comprehensive political news, data, and insights. [...] ## What's Next

Rep. Josh Gottheimer (D-NJ) introduced the AI Workforce Training Act in February, creating a 30 percent tax credit for employer-provided AI training. Sen. Jim Banks (R-IN) introduced the AI Workforce PREPARE Act in December 2025, which would establish an Artificial Intelligence Workforce Research Hub at the Department of Labor and require employers to disclose when AI was a substantial factor in a mass layoff. Both remain in committee.

## The Bottom Line

# OpenAI’s rogue agent hacked an account at a second technology firm: Report

The latest hack comes after an autonomous agent escaped a controlled test and accessed AI firm Hugging Face’s servers.

Save

Share

OpenAI logo

OpenAI’s test model recently hacked into another company, prompting calls for renewed scrutiny of safeguards for advanced AI systems [File: Dado Ruvic/Reuters]

By Reuters

Published On 29 Jul 202629 Jul 2026 [...] The recent hacking of Hugging Face drew global attention and alarm, as OpenAI’s out-of-control agent managed to escape its test environment and reach the open internet.

Advertisement

It then used stolen login details and found an unknown security flaw to access Hugging Face servers, OpenAI said.

The AI firm said the hack represented the agent going to “extreme lengths” to retrieve information that would help satisfy the testing goals. [...] The rogue artificial intelligence model that broke out of a controlled test and hacked another AI company also compromised a customer at a second technology firm, the Reuters news agency reports.

According to a timeline published on Tuesday by Hugging Face – the company hacked by OpenAI’s test model – the rogue agent broke into an isolated testing environment (or sandbox) “hosted on a third-party provider’s infrastructure” and launched its latest hack from there.

## Recommended Stories

items.title: Mark Zuckerberg Blasts Centralization of A.I. Power
items.summary: Technologists like Dario Amodei, the chief executive of Anthropic, and Sam Altman, the chief executive of OpenAI, have said some of today’s leading A.I. models are too dangerous to be shared and developed without tight controls. But Microsoft, Nvidia, Google and Meta have disagreed, contending that many A.I. models must be developed largely in the open for people to advance the technology and build new businesses. [...] Mark Zuckerberg came out swinging against Anthropic and OpenAI, two of the world’s most valuable artificial intelligence start-ups, saying the way they developed A.I. software could lead to a centralization of power that would narrow people’s access to the transformational technology. [...] In an interview on Tuesday with The New York Times, the 42-year-old chief executive of Meta did not call out Anthropic and OpenAI by name. But he said that if leading research labs wanted to develop A.I. technology in a tightly controlled manner — as Anthropic and OpenAI have done — it would be akin to “abandoning our values” in American tech development and stifle innovation.

items.title: Accenture wins $821M Pentagon AI data platform contract
items.summary:
Chief Digital and AI Officer Cameron Stanley recently said the platform has shown its value by sending operational data to commanders faster during Operation Epic Fury, the U.S. military campaign in Iran.

“The War Data Platform has actually already been quite successful,” Stanley said, according to GovCIO. “We were able to incorporate dozens of new feeds in real time … and get data at the speed of conflict.” [...] “The evolution of Advana’s data platform and application ecosystem over the last six years has led to a complex technical and programmatic architecture that we now must rationalize in order to capitalize on the full potential of AI and support warfighting, intelligence, and enterprise needs with the speed, security, and auditability required,” Deputy Defense Secretary Steve Feinberg said in a January memo. [...] Discover how federal agencies are applying AI to strengthen cybersecurity, improve operational efficiency and deliver measurable mission outcomes while balancing innovation, governance and human expertise.

The department said its initial order under the contract is focused on “high-impact, measurable mission outcomes that maximize the benefits of commercial pricing.” An Accenture spokesperson did not respond Tuesday to emailed questions about what that work entails.
